move: card slams up from below in 3D, live badge pulses, counter ticks
how: A dark card with a thumbnail, red LIVE pill, viewer count and two masked headline lines sits over a looping mp4 background (the timeline's onUpdate and a patched __fx.seek set video.currentTime). Both card and a back card start at y 900 / rotateX 18 / scale 0.9 and slam to place with expo.out over 0.9s (back card lags 0.1s and settles to y -22, scale 0.94); the front card gets an elastic.out(1,0.5) scaleY 1.06→1 overshoot. The LIVE pill pops with back.out(3), viewers slide in from x 60, headline lines rise yPercent 110→0 with expo.out stagger 0.08, the button pops back.out(2.5), and a red progress bar scaleX 0→1 runs linearly for D-1.5s. The LIVE dot yoyos scale 1→0.4 nine times, the viewer number counts 2,418→3,106 over 4s (power1.inOut) via a tweened object, and the headline gets a scale 1.03 hit at 50% with an elastic settle. Final 15%: text lines expo.in upward, then both cards fly to y -1100 with rotateX -12.
adapt: Swap the mp4 and thumbnail image, the show title lines, host names, date kicker and viewer numbers, and the red #ff2d2d accent; keep the 0.9s expo.out slam, the lagging back card and the 4s counter.
port: mount(el, shot) builds the card DOM plus the <video> and awaits loadeddata; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with the entrance at 0-0.2D, counter at 0.2-0.87D and exit at 0.85D. The video seek hack (patching window.__fx.seek) does not port: drive video.currentTime from a tween onUpdate on the returned timeline instead, and scope '.card', '.row span', '.n' to el.
caveats: background <video> is seeked by patching window.__fx.seek and via tl onUpdate; video seeking per frame is slow and may not be frame-exact
video.currentTime is wrapped modulo the clip length, so the background may cut mid-loop
backdrop-filter: blur(8px) on the viewers pill
